prompt:
Pixel art for a 16-bit style side-view arena shooter that runs at 640x360. Edit the attached template in place: it is drawn on a chunky pixel grid where one art pixel is exactly 1/240 of the image width; keep exactly that pixel size (never finer, never subdivided), and keep every size anchor and guide position. Crisp hard pixels: a clean 1-pixel near-black outline around every character, Enemy and prop; flat cel shading with 3-4 tones per material, shadows leaning purple-blue and highlights leaning warm yellow, light from the upper left; no anti-aliasing, no gradients, no blur, no soft edges, no semi-transparent pixels (use a checkerboard dither for any in-between tone). Characters are seen in a three-quarter side view (Metal Slug style): facing right, head and chest turned slightly toward the viewer. No text, no watermark, no shadows on the ground unless asked.

The attached image is a sheet of seven flat draft sprites for the Arena, a city plaza at sunset, on a pure #00FF00 green background, each with a white buffer around it. Redraw every sprite in place as crisp, finished, professional pixel art (modern commercial 16-bit quality), at exactly the same pixel size, position and outer size, so each one still fits its slot.

1) and 3) (top left and second row left): two one-way stone ledges the player stands on, 144 and 102 pixels wide. Each is a weathered mauve-grey stone slab: a bright warm sunlit top edge (the walkable surface, perfectly straight and flat along its whole length), a lip, a face of stone blocks with regular vertical joints, a little chipping and texture, a dark cool underside, and a small stepped stone corbel bracket under each end. A clean 1-pixel near-black outline all around. Both ledges are the same design, only the length differs.

2), 4), 5), 6), 7): five puffy sunset clouds of different sizes: soft rounded tops in cool mauve and violet, bellies lit from below by the setting sun in coral, peach and warm orange, with clean stepped pixel edges and a little checkerboard dither between the tones. Flat bottoms. No outline on the clouds.

Keep the pure #00FF00 background and the white buffer around each sprite. Nothing else on the sheet, no text.
